title: My Place: an old walk-up at the heart of SS15.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #416 | MY PLACE, SUBANG JAYA
excerpt: A low-density walk-up around a courtyard garden, surrounded by SS15's shops, colleges and international schools. Sean loves the layout and rental demand, but not the traffic, the exhaust or the resale outlook.
takeaways: A 900 sq ft three-bedroom unit sells for about RM400,000 to RM500,000 and rents for about RM2,500.
Every unit faces a central garden on one side and the street on the other, with two units per landing.
SS15's congestion, kitchen exhaust from shops behind and newer buildings nearby weigh on resale.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: My Place is a five-storey walk-up of a few hundred units in about three blocks set around a landscaped courtyard with a pool and ground-level parking, a rare use of land today. Each staircase serves only two units per floor and ten in all, so every unit has openings front and back, with living rooms and balconies facing the garden.

Sean viewed a 900 sq ft three-bedroom, two-bathroom unit with a 2.8 m ceiling, a large balcony, a separate kitchen and yard, old timber window frames and beams placed between rooms. The owner re-laid the piping, and The Makeover Guys refreshed the interior.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The block stands opposite INTI International College in SS15, among shop lots, cafes, clinics, education centres and two international schools, with Taylor's, Sunway and other colleges nearby. The LRT station is about 10 to 15 minutes' walk, the LDP, KESAS, MEX and Federal Highway are close, and Subang Parade is a little further. Parking is scarce at almost any hour.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: After its refresh, this unit rents for about RM2,500 a month, against about RM2,000 in a 2013 listing. Units sell for about RM400,000 to RM500,000, and rooms let for about RM700 to RM800 each, so renting room by room could reach about RM2,800 to RM3,000. Sean says long-term rent can cover the instalment.

standout.title: Everything faces the garden
standout.body: The blocks wrap a central courtyard and every living room and balcony looks inward, while bedrooms and kitchens get windows to the street. Surrounded by the backs of busy shop lots, the courtyard is what saves the building, and it gives each unit two-sided ventilation that modern double-loaded blocks rarely offer.

pros: SS15's location: at the centre of shopping, food, services and education, surrounded by the LDP, KESAS, MEX and Federal Highway, with the LRT about a 10-minute walk away.
The investment value: the location keeps an old design in demand, with tenants from office workers and students to blue-collar workers, whole-unit or room by room.
The density and design: a central garden with the blocks built around it, two units per landing, openings on two sides and sensible beam placement, which he calls a luxury today.
cons: The immediate setting: congestion almost all day, scarce parking and noise; school traffic once kept the junction jammed for about 40 minutes.
Old design standards: basic facilities, exposed drains, utilities that each owner has had to replace, and modest entrances, though an active management body allows sensible upgrades.
Upcoming projects: Subang Jaya's new developments will outshine older buildings, limiting resale value, while refurbishing costs and down payments make the return harder to justify.

closing: A nostalgic, high-demand rental near SS15's colleges; Sean would consider a first-floor unit, especially if his son studied nearby.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this December 2025 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view the refurbished unit; prices and rents are from listings and the owner as he quoted them. The Makeover Guys, where Sean works, refreshed the unit. He couldn't find the developer or original price.
